==========================================================================================

HRS 2007 Internet Release

Note to Users: This program is designed to create a codebook that matches the 
distribution dataset. Codebook content is derived from the data collection
system used to gather information for this study, e.g. Blaise. If you have any 
questions or suggestions concerning codebook layout or content please bring 
them to the attention of the HRS staff at hrsquest@isr.umich.edu.

Printing recommendation: Set margins (left/right/top/bottom) to .5 inch; print
in portrait orientation using a mono-space 10-point font.

==========================================================================================

I3_INTR1BALLQ       INTRO 1 BALL QUESTION A - INTRO
         Section: I     Level: RESPONDENT      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0
         Ref: Mod_5.SS003AB.intro

         Often people are uncertain about what their future Social Security might be. In
         the next question, we ask you to think about what your monthly benefits might
         be.
         
          We will show you 20 balls that you can put in seven different bins, reflecting
         what you think are the chances out of 20 that your future Social Security
         benefits fall in each bin. The more likely you think it is that your benefits
         fall in a given bin, the more balls you should assign to this bin.
         
          For example, if you put all the balls in the bin $500 - $800, it means you are
         certain that the amount you will receive is between $500 and $800.
         
          Another example is illustrated on the next screen.

I3_INTR2BALLQ1      INTRO 2 BALL QUESTION A - INTRO2
         Section: I     Level: RESPONDENT      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0
         Ref: Mod_5.SS003AB.intro2

         In this example, there are no balls in the ranges below $520 or above $1040, so
         it is certain that benefits will not be lower than $520 or higher than $1040.
         
          12 out of 20 balls are in the bin $520 - $780 meaning that the chance that
         benefits are between $520 and $780 is 12 out of 20 (60 percent).
         
          There is a smaller chance, 8 out of 20 (40 percent), that benefits are between
         $780 and $1040.
         
          Of course this is just an example to illustrate; the chances you have in mind
         may be completely different.
         
          Now it's your turn! Choose next to start allocating balls.

         .................................................................................
            65           1.  ASKED BALL QUESTIONS
          2600       Blank.  INAP (Inapplicable) or Data Missing


==========================================================================================

I3_BALLNUM1_1       ASSIGNED BALL NUMBER-1-1
         Section: I     Level: RESPONDENT      Type: Numeric    Width: 4   Decimals: 0
         Ref: Mod_5.SS003AB.FLTresh1

         User Note: The value in the BALLNUM variables represents the endpoint of the
         range of values that was assigned to each bin. The ranges are calculated using
         the following formula: If the R provides an amount at SS003A_NEWAMOUNT, or
         SS003A_AMOUNT (see Ref) if there is data in both variables, the length (L) of
         the interval of one bin is L=A/3.5 (rounded down to the nearest 5) and the
         thresholds would be: 0, L, 2L, 3L, 4L 5L, 6L . For example, if
         SS003A_AMOUNT=800, the values for the BALLNUM series would be 0, 225, 450, 675,
         900, 1125, 1350. Thus, the bin ranges would be 0-225 for Bin 1, 225-450 for Bin
         2, 450-675 for Bin 3, 675-900 for Bin 4, 900-1125 for Bin 5, 1125-1350 for Bin
         6, and more than 1350 for Bin 7 (see Ref).

         .................................................................................
            65           0.  Actual Value
          2600       Blank.  INAP (Inapplicable) or Data Missing

I3_BINSNUM_A        ASSIGNED NUMBER OF BINS-1
         Section: I     Level: RESPONDENT      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0
         Ref: Mod_5.Bins_A

         User Note: This variable determines the number of bins presented.  Below are the
         rules for how BINS_A and BINSIZE_A (see Ref) are assigned:
         
         delta := L2_A - L1_A
             if delta >= 300 and delta < 450 then
               BINS_A := 2
               RoundToFive(delta/2, BINSIZE_A)
             else if delta >= 450 and delta < 600 then
               BINS_A := 3
               RoundToFive(delta/3, BINSIZE_A)
             else if delta >= 600 and delta < 750 then
               BINS_A := 4
               RoundToFive(delta/4, BINSIZE_A)
             else if delta >= 750 then
               BINS_A := 5
               RoundToFive(delta/5, BINSIZE_A)

I3_BALLINTRO5       INTRO 1 BALL QUESTION D - INTRO
         Section: I     Level: RESPONDENT      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0
         Ref: Mod_5.SS003BB.intro

         Often people are uncertain about what their future Social Security might be. In
         the next question, we ask you to think about what your monthly benefits might
         be.
         
          We will show you 20 balls that you can put in seven different bins, reflecting
         what you think are the chances out of 20 that your future Social Security
         benefits fall in each bin. The more likely you think it is that your benefits
         fall in a given bin, the more balls you should assign to this bin.
         
          For example, if you put all the balls in the bin $500 - $800, it means you are
         certain that the amount you will receive is between $500 and $800.
         
          Another example is illustrated on the next screen.

         .................................................................................
           320           1.  ASKED BALL QUESTIONS
          2345       Blank.  INAP (Inapplicable) or Data Missing

I3_INTR2BALLQ2      INTRO 2 BALL QUESTION D - INTRO2
         Section: I     Level: RESPONDENT      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0
         Ref: Mod_5.SS003BB.intro2

         In this example, there are no balls in the ranges below $520 or above $1040, so
         it is certain that benefits will not be lower than $520 or higher than $1040.
         
          12 out of 20 balls are in the bin $520 - $780 meaning that the chance that
         benefits are between $520 and $780 is 12 out of 20 (60 percent).
         
          There is a smaller chance, 8 out of 20 (40 percent), that benefits are between
         $780 and $1040.
         
          Of course this is just an example to illustrate; the chances you have in mind
         may be completely different.
         
          Now it's your turn! Choose next to start allocating balls.

I3_BALLNUM1_5       ASSIGNED BALL NUMBER-1-5
         Section: I     Level: RESPONDENT      Type: Numeric    Width: 6   Decimals: 0
         Ref: Mod_5.SS003BB.FLTresh1

         User Note: The value in the BALLNUM variables represents the endpoint of the
         range of values that was assigned to each bin. The ranges are calculated using
         the following formula: If the R provides an amount at SS003B_NEWAMOUNT, or
         SS003B_AMOUNT (see Ref) if there is data in both variables, the length (L) of
         the interval of one bin is L=A/3.5 (rounded down to the nearest 5) and the
         thresholds would be: 0, L, 2L, 3L, 4L 5L, 6L . For example, if
         SS003B_AMOUNT=800, the values for the BALLNUM series would be 0, 225, 450, 675,
         900, 1125, 1350. Thus, the bin ranges would be 0-225 for Bin 1, 225-450 for Bin
         2, 450-675 for Bin 3, 675-900 for Bin 4, 900-1125 for Bin 5, 1125-1350 for Bin
         6, and more than 1350 for Bin 7 (see Ref).

         .................................................................................
           321           0.  Actual Value
          2344       Blank.  INAP (Inapplicable) or Data Missing

I3_BINSNUM_B        ASSIGNED NUMBER OF BINS-2
         Section: I     Level: RESPONDENT      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0
         Ref: Mod_5.Bins_B

         User Note: This variable determines the number of bins presented. Below are the
         rules for how BINS_B and BINSIZE_B (see Ref) are assigned:
                 
                  delta := L2_B - L1_B
                      if delta >= 300 and delta < 450 then
                        BINS_B := 2
                        RoundToFive(delta/2, BINSIZE_B)
                      else if delta >= 450 and delta < 600 then
                        BINS_B := 3
                        RoundToFive(delta/3, BINSIZE_B)
                      else if delta >= 600 and delta < 750 then
                        BINS_B := 4
                        RoundToFive(delta/4, BINSIZE_B)
                      else if delta >= 750 then
                        BINS_B := 5
                        RoundToFive(delta/5, BINSIZE_B)

         .................................................................................
           154                     2-5.  Actual Value
          2511                   Blank.  INAP (Inapplicable) or Data Missing

I3_INTROU7          INTRO 1 BALL QUESTION E - INTRO
         Section: I     Level: RESPONDENT      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0
         Ref: Mod_5.SP1_2_2.intro

         Often people are uncertain about when they will start collecting their Social
         Security benefits. In the next question, we ask you about the age at which you
         will start collecting these benefits.
         
          On the next screen we will show you 20 balls that you can put in eight
         different bins. Each bin stands for a particular age. Please put the balls in
         the bins to show the chances that you will start collecting at each age. The
         more likely a particular age, the more balls you should assign to that age.
         
          For example, if age 63 is most likely you should put more balls in bin 63 than
         in any other bin.

         .................................................................................
